title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (Longue Marche notes, around the birational and higher-dimensional section conjecture). K is a field, L/K a function field, U a smooth K-variety with function field L, and X a regular compactification with X \ U = D = ∪_{i∈I} D_i a normal-crossings divisor. For x ∈ X\U, I(x) ⊂ I is the set of branches through x. Ũ_x is the punctured local scheme (henselian or strict henselisation) of X at x, restricted to U. Its geometric fundamental group, i.e. the inertia I_x, is (the tame part of) T̂^{I(x)} ≅ Ẑ(1)^{I(x)}.

The previous page asks two questions.
- 1°) Is π1(Ũ_x) → π1(U) injective? Equivalently, does I_x ≅ T̂^{I(x)} inject into the geometric group Π_{U/K}?
- 2°) Let V be a valuation of L/K whose residue field is algebraic over K (a dimension-zero point of the Zariski–Riemann-type space X_{L/K}), centred at x. Is the decomposition group N_V → N_x open, i.e. is I_V → I_x surjective?

This page first comments on the two questions. 2° is purely local around x and 'should be essentially trivial', whether the presumption turns out true or false. 1° is global over U and in no way trivial.

It then draws the consequence. Take a section s of the extension 1 → Π^{L̄}_{L/K} → E^{L̄}_U (or the birational group) → G_K coming from a valuation of L/K with residue field K. If 1° and 2° hold, s(G_K) lands in the decomposition group N_x of the centre x and normalises the inertia subgroup Δ_x ≅ T̂^{I(x)} of the geometric group. This Δ_x is nontrivial exactly when the valuation has no centre on U, i.e. when the section is not attached to a K-rational point of U. Grothendieck notes this is 'precisely one of the senses' of the §2 conjectures, which 'seem at first implausible'.

In modern terms: sections at infinity are cuspidal / boundary sections. They are characterised by normalising a nontrivial inertia torus Ẑ(1)^d, whereas sections coming from points of U do not. This is the group-theoretic way to separate 'points at infinity' from 'genuine points' in a section conjecture for U and for its birational version.

The page ends announcing a closer study of the I_x ⊂ Π̄_{L/K}, and of the normaliser/centraliser questions for N_v, I_v, before returning to 1° and 2°.
errors: Question 1° (injectivity of the local inertia T̂^{I(x)} into the global geometric π1(U)) is false in general when card I(x) ≥ 2, as Grothendieck's own margin note on the previous page says. Example: U = P^2 minus two lines = A^1 × G_m has geometric π1 ≅ Ẑ(1), while the local group at the crossing point is Ẑ(1)^2. So the implication drawn on this page only holds as stated for card I(x)=1, e.g. for curves.

For card I(x) ≥ 2 one must replace Δ_x by the image of I_x in Π. Its nontriviality when the valuation has no centre on U then needs a separate argument, e.g. a hyperbolicity or 'good' hypothesis on U.
In positive characteristic, T̂^{I(x)} should be the tame (prime-to-p) inertia; the page tacitly works in characteristic 0 or tamely.

ideas.what: Local π1 at a normal-crossings boundary point is T̂^{I(x)} (Ẑ(1)^d), and its map to the global π1(U).
ideas.modern_name: Abhyankar's lemma / tame inertia at normal crossings divisors

ideas.what: Sections coming from valuations with residue field K that are centred on the boundary normalise a nontrivial inertia group Ẑ(1)^{I(x)}, distinguishing them from sections coming from K-rational points of U.
ideas.modern_name: cuspidal (boundary) sections; group-theoretic characterisation of decomposition and inertia groups at cusps; birational section conjecture
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (letter to Faltings 1983); later Nakamura, Mochizuki, Tamagawa, Koenigsmann, Pop, Stix (2000s)
ideas.where_published: Letter to Faltings (1983) for curves and cuspidal sections; the higher-dimensional normal-crossings version is perhaps only in these notes

ideas.what: Comparing decomposition and inertia groups of valuations of rank/dimension zero with those of their centre x (is I_V → I_x surjective?).
ideas.modern_name: decomposition and inertia groups of valuations versus divisorial/point inertia
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical valuation theory; Pop and Koenigsmann for Galois-theoretic recovery of valuations

missed.claim: A higher-dimensional criterion for sections over a variety U with normal-crossings boundary: a section coming from a valuation with residue field K is 'at infinity' iff its image normalises a nontrivial inertia torus Δ_x ≅ Ẑ(1)^{I(x)}. Grothendieck flags that the needed global injectivity (1°) is nontrivial and, by his own margin, false for multiple crossings.
missed.quote: l'image de E_K^{L̄} doit normaliser un sous-groupe Δ_x ≃ T̂^{I(x)} de π_{L/K}^{L̄}, qui est non trivial si la valuation n'a pas de centre sur U
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Higher-dimensional and birational section conjecture work (Stix, Pop, Esnault–Wittenberg) handles cuspidal sections mainly for curves. The precise failure of inertia injectivity at multiple crossings, and its effect on detecting boundary sections, is a modest point that is rarely spelled out.

deep.surprise_reason: These are working notes, and the characterisation of cuspidal sections via normalised inertia is known in spirit (letter to Faltings, later anabelian literature). The higher-dimensional normal-crossings formulation and the self-diagnosed failure of injectivity are interesting details, but not a striking new result.
